H4LA05171.name: Peter Williams
H4LA05171.bio: Owner since 1999 of Resource One Nursery, a family tree farm and specialty crop business in Lettsworth; former public school teacher.

positions.stance: Holds as a conservative principle "marriage between one man and one woman."
Holds as a conservative principle "the right to own and bear arms."
Holds as a conservative principle "the constitutional right to legally vote."
Expresses "compassion for the poor, sick, women and children, disabled veterans, and others that depend on federal and state safety net programs."
Will "fight and support small business development in underserved areas," especially federal Opportunity Zones in Baton Rouge, New Orleans East and surrounding rural communities.

H6LA03148.name: Clay Higgins
H6LA03148.bio: Served in Acadiana law enforcement, including as a Lafayette deputy marshal, and as a U.S. Army military police officer.

wiki:kate-cotten.name: Kate Cotten
wiki:kate-cotten.bio: Raised in her family's business, Cotten's Burgers in Lake Charles.

positions.stance: Will fight "the gutting of our national parks: no selling them off, no starving them of rangers and funding."
"No new wars. No further military intervention in Iran."
Says the debt has passed $37 trillion and will "vote against any budget that grows the debt without a plan to pay it down."
Personally "100% pro-life" but "would not vote in favor of an abortion ban"; supports counseling, waiting periods, and support for mothers and children.
Supports paid sick leave, maternity and paternity leave, universal pre-K and Head Start, school meals, daycare tax credits, and affordable healthcare.

H6LA03205.name: John Day
H6LA03205.bio: U.S. Navy veteran (1994–1998) who worked in business, insurance, finance and hurricane recovery, and is now a professional writer.

positions.stance: Wants to cut everyday costs and "lower insurance premiums and stop unfair rate hikes," increasing competition to bring prices down.
"Bring good-paying jobs back to Louisiana," support small businesses, and invest in job training, trades, and apprenticeships.
"Enforce the law and secure the border," stop fentanyl trafficking, and "fix a broken system with clear, legal pathways."
"Protect your right to make your own medical decisions," expand rural care, keep hospitals funded, and lower prescription drug costs.
"Defend Social Security and Medicare benefits" with "no cuts to earned benefits."

H4LA03135.name: Priscilla Gonzalez
H4LA03135.bio: Former Herrman & Herrman employee in Corpus Christi and 2021 candidate for mayor of Corpus Christi.

positions.stance: Dedicated to "a fair and equitable justice system that prioritizes rehabilitation over punishment."
Offers strategies for "job creation, supporting small businesses, and fostering sustainable economic growth."
Says "investing in education and workforce development is crucial for our district's success."
Criticizes the Louisiana House's vote against SB26, describing it as a measure to secure increased funding for public schools.
Committed to "increasing teacher salaries and ensuring they receive the respect and compensation they deserve."

wiki:caleb-walker.name: Caleb Walker
wiki:caleb-walker.bio: Ten-year U.S. Army veteran who rose to Sergeant First Class, and former Sam's Club department manager.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower the cost of groceries, housing, insurance, healthcare and other necessities while supporting better wages.
Will fight "for wages and pay raises that keep pace with today's economy."
Will increase teacher pay and "make the first $50,000 of every educator's salary exempt from federal income tax."
Will "provide student-loan forgiveness for healthcare workers who serve Louisiana families."
Will "secure hazardous-duty pay for essential workers required to serve during declared natural disasters."

H6LA04138.name: Mike Johnson
H6LA04138.bio: Speaker of the U.S. House and U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 4th District since 2017; former state legislator and constitutional law attorney.

H6LA04187.name: Conrad Cable
H6LA04187.bio: First-generation farmer in Union Parish and ULM graduate.

positions.stance: Says a $17 minimum by 2030 "is not enough"; workers "deserve a wage that rises with inflation each year."
Pledges to "protect union rights, strengthen worker protections, and make work fair, safe, and dignified for everyone."
Opposes the $2.13 tipped minimum wage, saying "we must ensure a living wage for all workers."
Supports Medicare for All, saying "Healthcare should depend on need, not income."
"We must protect Medicare and Medicaid so everyone can get care when they need it."
"We must make living affordable again" by lowering housing, grocery, gas, utility and childcare costs.
Proposes the START program, investing in early childhood education with licensed educators instead of families paying about $13,000 a year for childcare.
Proposes a Small Business Wage Bridge Act raising the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour while shifting corporate subsidies to small businesses.
"Our schools must be funded, our teachers must be paid, and our communities must have a say."
Supports expanding school meal programs so "all students get three meals a day with dignity."

H6LA04229.name: Gordan Heslop
H6LA04229.bio: Retired accounting professor at Northwestern State University of Louisiana and East Texas A&M University.

positions.stance: "Abolish the tariffs."
Would "remove the current limit on earnings subject to social security tax" to address the program's approaching funding shortage.
"Focus on the health of the rural economy."
"Provide preventative health screening," including a voluntary yearly blood test for adults.
Proposes "a massive first home program - not costing the government anything."

H6LA05184.name: Stewart Cathey Jr.
H6LA05184.bio: Louisiana state senator for District 33 since 2019, U.S. Army officer and engineer, and management consulting small business owner.

H6LA05200.name: Misti Cordell
H6LA05200.bio: Healthcare consulting business owner and former Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents.

positions.stance: Will protect agriculture, energy and local businesses "by cutting red tape, lowering taxes, and standing up to federal overreach."
"I'll cut taxes, slash federal waste, end job-killing regulations, and defend our small businesses and workers."
"I'll back our law enforcement, protect your Second Amendment rights, and restore law and order."
"I'll secure the border, finish the wall, stop illegal immigration, shut down the cartels, and put Louisiana workers first."
Will "fight for school choice, oppose woke indoctrination, and return education to local communities."

H6LA05242.name: Michael Echols
H6LA05242.bio: Louisiana state representative for District 14, licensed contractor, and commercial real estate investor and builder.

positions.stance: Congress should focus on "lowering inflation, expanding domestic energy production, and removing federal regulations that drive up the cost of rebuilding."
"Rein in Washington's reckless spending, expand American energy production to lower fuel costs, and remove unnecessary regulations."
Supports "rebuilding America's military, standing with Israel as it defends itself against terrorism, and confronting the Iranian regime."
"Any immigrant caught defrauding American taxpayers should be denaturalized and deported"; illegal immigrants should be barred from taxpayer-funded benefits.
"We must secure the border, end the policies that encourage illegal immigration," while strengthening legal immigration.

H6LA05317.name: Gabe Firment
H6LA05317.bio: Louisiana state representative since 2019, chairman of the House Insurance Committee, and small business owner.

positions.stance: Will "protect American sovereignty, uphold the rule of law, and keep our communities safe."
Will "unleash American energy production, create good-paying jobs, and lower costs for families and businesses."
Will "defend our agricultural economy, preserve our way of life, and ensure prosperity for future generations."
Will "honor commitments to Americans and ensure these programs remain strong for future generations."
Will "support local jobs, strengthen rural economies, and ensure responsible stewardship of our forests."

H6LA05283.name: Austin Magee
H6LA05283.bio: Owner of Pittman Industrial, a welding and mechanical company.

H6LA05341.name: Patricia Moore
H6LA05341.bio: Louisiana state representative for House District 17 since 2019.

positions.stance: "I will work to lower everyday costs, support fair wages, make childcare more affordable, and help create good jobs."
Says every part of the district, including rural parishes and small towns, "deserves to be seen and served."
Supports small businesses, skilled trades, workforce training, agriculture and new industries "that create good-paying jobs close to home."
"Our children deserve good schools. Teachers deserve our support."
Supports protecting rural hospitals, more affordable healthcare, lower medicine costs, mental and behavioral healthcare, and care seniors have earned.

H6LA05325.name: Antonio Wilson
H6LA05325.bio: Licensed general contractor and business owner from Tallulah.

positions.stance: Pledges to return calls and connect residents with government resources, treating "every concern like a work order on a job site."
Will recruit employers in manufacturing, logistics, agriculture processing, healthcare and technology, and tie federal training dollars to local hiring commitments.
Will push for federal policies and funding to keep rural hospitals and clinics open, attract doctors and nurses, and expand telemedicine.
Will create "a public accountability dashboard" showing federal funding pursued, funded projects, timelines and status.
Advocates improvements in "water and sewer systems, roads, bridges, drainage, housing, broadband, and more."

H6LA06158.name: Monique Appeaning
H6LA06158.bio: More than 25 years of public service in Louisiana's executive and legislative branches, including as a budget analyst for the Louisiana National Guard.

positions.stance: "Back the Blue" and "crack down on violent crime and trafficking."
"Strengthen and modernize our military" and "keep America the strongest force in the world."
"Large tax cuts for hardworking people," with no tax on tips, overtime, or Social Security.
"Stop outsourcing and rebuild American manufacturing."
"Protect Louisiana farmers and defend American agriculture."
"Support small business, expand workforce training, and attract good-paying jobs."
"Invest in our schools, support teachers, and create pathways for student success."
"Protect and expand access to affordable, quality healthcare for all families."

H6LA05168.name: Larry Davis
H6LA05168.bio: Licensed minister and middle-class worker from Livingston Parish.

positions.stance: Supports lowering costs for families and small businesses, reducing federal spending, deregulation, and "pro-job tax policy."
"Strong border enforcement, physical barriers where necessary, crackdown on cartels, mandatory employment verification, and tightening asylum loopholes."
Supports police, increased penalties for violent crime, federal support against human trafficking, and fentanyl enforcement.
Parents as "the primary decision makers in children's education"; supports curriculum transparency, school choice and vocational programs.
"Increase domestic drilling, expand refining capacity, support nuclear advancement, reduce regulatory burden on energy producers."

H6LA05226.name: Rick Edmonds
H6LA05226.bio: Louisiana state senator representing the Baton Rouge area, with prior service in ministry and education.

positions.stance: "Protect Louisiana jobs and fight to make life more affordable."
"Strengthen Louisiana's energy industry and protect energy jobs."
"Back the Blue and stand with law enforcement."
"Cut wasteful spending and get Washington off Louisiana's back."
"Protect access to critical flood insurance and disaster relief."

H6LA06190.name: Pat Forbes
H6LA06190.bio: Has spent 20 years leading Louisiana's recovery and rebuilding after Katrina, Gustav, the 2016 floods and other disasters.

positions.stance: "I'll back real rules against price-fixing and the enforcement to make them stick."
Says the war with Iran is raising fuel prices and Congress should be "a check on the President, not a rubber stamp."
"End the tariffs. They are a tax on everything you buy."
Supports lowering premiums by reducing risk through stronger Fortified roofs, elevated houses and drainage.
Will push for disclosure of insurers' collections, payouts and assumptions when they seek rate increases.

H6LA05309.name: Lindsay Garcia
H6LA05309.bio: Former New Orleans secondary social studies teacher (2010–2020) and former Department of Defense recreation specialist.

positions.stance: Protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, lower prescription costs, raise wages, expand housing and childcare, and support small businesses.
Bring federal dollars home for I-10 and I-12, bridges, roads, drainage, flood protection, water and sewer systems, and affordable flood insurance.
Grow manufacturing, energy, construction, technology, healthcare and skilled-trade jobs while expanding apprenticeships, technical training, early education and teacher support.
"Ensure clean air and water, responsible energy development, strong property-rights protections, rural investment, affordable broadband and better access to healthcare."
Fight violent crime, trafficking and fentanyl while supporting fair justice, constitutional policing, voting rights, civil rights and due process.

H6LA05259.name: Michael Mebruer
H6LA05259.bio: LSU graduate with a master's in financial economics who has worked as a traveling medical professional.

positions.stance: Supports "restructuring major entitlement programs," simplifying the tax code, and reducing federal bureaucracy to restore fiscal discipline.
Believes "every human life has inherent dignity and value" and supports policies that protect the unborn.
Supports "mandatory nationwide implementation of the E-Verify system" and penalties for employers who knowingly hire illegal workers.
Supports moving Medicare toward competing private plans and restructuring Medicaid to give states more flexibility.
Supports "comprehensive tax reform that simplifies the tax code and reduces the overall tax burden on American workers."

H6LA05234.name: Blake Miguez
H6LA05234.bio: Louisiana state senator since 2023, former House Republican Majority Leader, and manager of his family's oil and gas business.

positions.stance: "In Washington he'll push term limits and a permanent ban on members trading individual stocks."
Will work to lower electricity, housing, grocery, insurance and healthcare costs.
Will "cut the taxes and federal red tape that drive employers out" and back trades and technical training.
Will "finish the wall, fund the agents, end catch-and-release, mandate E-Verify," and treat cartels as foreign terrorist organizations.
Will fight to approve LNG export permits, "stop the slow-walking of Gulf leasing," and push permitting reform.

H6LA06182.name: Stephen Wagley
H6LA06182.bio: Chief Operating Officer of Delta College, a family-owned proprietary school that trains healthcare workers.

positions.stance: Will "move to censure and strip committee assignments from any member who supports terrorist organizations or calls for replacing our Constitution."
"Life begins at conception"; will fight to make sure "none of our tax dollars fund Planned Parenthood."
Will fight to keep the Trump tax cuts permanent, simplify the tax code, and oppose new federal regulations and mandates.
Calls to stop federal overspending and unleash American energy: "I will never vote for a new regulation unless another one has been erased."
Will support President Trump's mission "in building the wall, fighting the Cartels and criminals."
